flags.shown: Acerola visits the Mimikyu on Tuesdays.
After the fall, they're an applicant at Specialist.
The next fire opens with it.
They're asked next time.
He asks first, always.
"They ask if I'm all right."
A month's waiver on the Board; a photograph for the Wall.
A back way, free, for this region's base.
Funds, a little. Neither column.
The bakery offers a half share, next district.
The neighbour's opinion +1; Given +2.
The basement's left alone. Noticing: Open.
A Dig's Site, free.
That Pokémon sits out whenever the Hero's the opponent.
It uses no move against the Hero's team.
A Work: a bed at the Clinic.
His note on it's the best paragraph in the Scheme log.
The Sit-Down's table gains a fact.
"Since then: went home. With Tam."
Their Pokémon's Bond +1.
"You learn what the numbers are about."
A fallen Boss on the Roster, at ₽150, with a line.
A Work in the old district every few days, unsigned.
What the Roster calls the Boss on every card.
The Boss runs the Pen and writes "Since then".
A sealed bottle on the Common Room shelf, for the run.
"There's doors that want standing in at a café."
A Scout of the whole canal, free.
A Front on the Board tomorrow, a third cheaper.
A cat. It likes whoever's mood is lowest.
"Offered me a chair. Twice."
Kits recover a day faster again, for the region.
A child in the base. Never on a job, a door or in a kit.
Their odds +10% for good, after one practice battle.
It's in the box, listed: "her mum's".
The woman's in the count at the Notice.
A constable eats in the Mess once. She's the warning before a Raid.
The door Grunt gave them the corridor floor anyway.
An applicant. Flaw: Freezes. Loyalty 8.
They notice first if the Ledger says a different Creed.
One word of the Creed's line may be changed.
It's back. Whoever hid it knocks next.
An applicant, with a line already written.
Taken in at the door if it's Belonging.
Stored: why us.
The detective knows the Boss was warned.
The Dig stops. The clean way's opened.
No Common Room door. Hear someone out is free there.
A door that shuts. A feud mends behind it.
It's the Doubts line in the last room.
Chidi's sentence on the Scheme screen.
An apology in person by the Executive; Taken −3, put back.
They ask. Something's lost, once, while they're asking.
Executives waive, one a district.
Given +2; the neighbour's opinion +1, even at War.
Faye may be asked at Hear someone out.
She asks Lux.
It was Faye.
Mended by morning behind a door, or a week in the open.
The thing's on the Office desk one Night, then the Vault.
The flaw's struck through on their card.
A Sit-Down with Lysandre, forced.
A fourth channel between the two sides, carrying nothing.
Scout jobs +15%, never as the signal.
The Friend knows who the Boss is.
A room furnished by trades. Free.
They come back. The district's held by nobody.
The garrison does one small Work a district, free.
Thief and Covet skip held items that are gifts.
The kit's one short. The girl's got a Rattata.
Hand down: a TM, not a Pokémon, offered once.
Hear someone out, on them, tonight: free.
The heist's way in changes.
The Boss's one letter to the Hero may answer it.
A saucer on the Hero's fire.
Stored: "My mother."
He comes back twice, for the sandwich.
He's given the address of Skull's Home.
The Card's Not-known field carries his initials.
The Pen's latch opens from inside.
The headline: "BOTH."
The piece is kind. Six weeks on: "WHAT THEY DIDN'T SAY".
The piece is a guess.
His mother writes to the Front's address. The Post won't open it.
Kit Pokémon lose their numbers.
A Work: the kitchen.
He's the first name on the detective's list.
He comes to Sunday's singing.
She's still furious.
The Mess does the laundry properly from now.
A Work: a laundry. A job against Plasma with her name on it.
That Card, next time: +5% with this Lead.
It's the Leader's line at the gate on the Reckoning's last day.
The base is a lease, clean.
The Board has leave, and a job that fits.
A correction in the Ledger, initialled, dated, left visible.
Lied to a child.
The Line slips a step, in the Log.
Every lock in Galar opens for the boat. Reach +2.
The locksmith: persuade him and Hands +10% on locks.
Machines kits: the squad's lowest rank may halt a job.
The trainer's holding is one mood warmer.
They can be made Officer.
This knock returns, till it's sat with.
A Mimikyu: Raid squads who meet it lose a turn.
A Misdreavus at the edge of the Hero's party.

A slip in the mole file: "Hortense: unsure."
His line on the Monday.
Her mood's floor is Easy.
The Hero's mother comes up every few days. Her mood starts Warm.
One name off the list for each Kind who knocks.
Giovanni: "You've taken them. Good."
"Won't" becomes "Never".
A battle, three each, at level: the Night's action. His kit tier +1.
He's the second person not clapping, if the Speech is "only the good".
Otis lets him past in District 5, and denies it.
A line on their card: "Won't be in the room."
The Hero's home street is off the Post's list.
They can't be made Officer this region.
The Roster's own post and calls aren't opened.
Tomorrow's job there: −20%, and the Card says why.
The detective's list never has her name on it.
Off the Roster for three days.
On deck the whole way at a Crossing; never on the staying list.
Otis stands outside the Vault for the run, facing out.
Otis has been letting them use his mug.
Otis's Loyalty +1.
A Patron (or a second one). She funds a room.
One job at the pair's bonus. If it lands, they're a pair.
The Pen is handed to someone they named.
Pen cards are corrected with names.
"She talks to the Pidgey."
The Scheme screen's sentence gets plainer a step early.
She walks. Eleven miles.
A promise. Broken: Loyalty −2, theirs.
He'll be seen again.
The Roster's lines read a little differently.
They pull the punch in the neighbour's next war job.
Hired. Talent: "Persistent."
This knock returns, three times.
The Roster likes the Rival.
The Rival's tier moves; the Hero hears.
"They walk into places on their own."
A ruling's kept. The heir's first quarrel's judged by it.
"It didn't mind that I was scared."
Stored: their line about the sea.
A second photograph on the Wall, if one's pinned.
A cat in the Garage. Everyone knows but the Boss.
You know a secret. So do they, by morning.
The shop tips to the team by itself two districts on.
The one shunt, used.
Heat for having a base stays nil.
The Card's Not-known field: "What the Slugma know."
A job against Snag'em on the Board.
A Work, backdated to Arrival: the shelter.
"Respectable" trebles. The Roster are staff when she's about.
Sandwiches on the step, every few days.
The Scheme screen's sentence gets plainer.
₽800 a day, kept.
The stipend stops.
The sentence is their card's top line.
The Stray's read a Card. The Hero's told.
The Stray's search moves a step.
Two tickets for the Battle Subway.
The surplus sits. She asks again at ₽50,000.
The kit screen shows nicknames for Swarm kits.
flags.readBy: The Hero's File: "Them again. One's called Gerald"

flags.shown: Moved to a job that uses their talent.
Talks is an ear: one thing a district, as a trade.
He tells the Hero the truth at his door, unprompted.
The neighbour's own Talks, named; hireable at a Truce.
He tells one tick's job a day early.
The base can't be found by an inspection.
She carries a tin mug to drop.
A knock next district if it's not mended.
A back way, and he knows it too.
A hand-sewn flag, wrong colour.
An applicant: no talent shown, Loyalty 7 on day one.
A job tonight with no Card. Skull's stance: Understanding.
The Vault's moved one square, and it's better.
The thing's out of play.
Corruption doesn't rise this district.
"She'd my mother's hands."
Their wage doubles. Somebody else hears.
"The Boss's wage: lent."
Loyalty's floor for the region: 4.
₽14 a head. Old Obadiah frames his.
The waiver's struck from the Given column.
A custom: a new hire's walked round by a Lead on day one.
The Wall: "edited".
The Warden: Persuade free for the region.
Defend with a day's warning: the back way's count doubles.
Heat 9's warning a day early, with a fifth choice.
They watch the heir stand at the window.
Their quest, a step.
What they see from the window, stored.
She stands with the Witness while they read.
It's in the Common Room; the Hero's File mentions only it.
The day's worst job gets an undo on tomorrow's Board.
"Somebody I was writing to's stopped." Temper +1.
A Grunt steps into one of the Hero's fights with the neighbour.
A van, very slowly, and cones, in the yard of an Evening.

knocks.title: Swarm: “Is that all we're for?”
knocks.says: (A Grunt with three Rattata.) “The kid beat all three with one move. One. I've had them since they were that big. Is that all we're for? Being three?”

answers.reply: “Pip. Other Pip. And Gerald.”

answers.say: Three's the point. One gets through.
answers.reply: “None got through.” (They go on being three.)
“No. I want these to be enough.”

knocks.title: Bruisers: the Machop
knocks.says: “I won. Fair. He shook my hand. Then his Machop wouldn't look at him. I did that. I didn't think about the Machop.”

answers.say: Go back tomorrow. Take a Potion.
answers.reply: “For the Machop?” “For the Machop.”
“Then I'd like it to feel more like it.”
“…He looked pleased. I felt worse.”

knocks.title: Tricksters: the Amulet Coin
knocks.says: “I took her Persian's Amulet Coin mid-fight. It's the Doctrine. It's also her mum's.”

answers.reply: “With a note?” “No note.” “…I'm putting a note.”

answers.say: It's in the box. It's ours.
answers.reply: “It's in the box. It's hers.”

answers.say: Take items in fights. Not keepsakes.
answers.reply: “How do I tell?” “You'll know.” “I did know. That's why I'm here.”

knocks.title: Beasts: half a sandwich
knocks.says: “He won't fight the kid any more. Just sits. She gave him half a sandwich last week. I'm not cross. I'm asking what I do.”

answers.say: Don't send him at the kid.
answers.reply: “And if she's at my door?” “Then you'll stand at it without him.”
“He doesn't, though. That's what I'm telling you.”
“…Egg.” (The Mess makes egg sandwiches.)

knocks.title: Machines: the plan was wrong
knocks.says: “They do exactly what's on the plan. I wrote the plan. Today the plan was wrong and none of them stopped.”

answers.reply: “Who presses it?” “Whoever's nearest.”
“I will. I'd hoped for more than that.”
“Went through a wall that had somebody's kitchen behind it. Nobody hurt. A dresser.”

knocks.title: Ghosts: the Misdreavus
knocks.says: “My Misdreavus has been following the kid. At night. Not for us. I think it likes her.”

answers.reply: “It'll tell me things.” “Don't ask it.”
“It'll know I'm using it.”
“She's left a saucer out.”

knocks.title: Tide: someone from inland
knocks.says: (A Grunt from inland.) “I'd never seen the sea. You gave me a Tentacool. I've seen it now. I think about it.”

answers.say: Go down tomorrow. Take the morning.
answers.reply: “The whole morning?”
“That it doesn't stop. I'd assumed it stopped somewhere.”

answers.say: It's a Tentacool. Don't get soft.
answers.reply: “Too late.”

knocks.title: Ember: the second wall
knocks.says: “It's warm down there and it shouldn't be. The Slugma won't go past the second wall. They like warm.”

answers.reply: “That's the Scheme's Place, past that wall.” “I know what it is.”
“Which one?” (They wait.)

answers.say: What do you think it is?
answers.reply: “I think it's asleep and we're a draught.”

knocks.title: “What's it for?”
knocks.says: “We made more than we need this week. That's not happened before. I've come to ask what it's for.”

answers.reply: “That's an answer. It's not a use.” (She asks again at ₽50,000, in the same words.)
“By how much?” (A tenth, or a quarter. Once.)

answers.say: What would you do with it?
answers.reply: “Buy the cannery and run it properly. I've seen their books. They're a disgrace.”

knocks.title: The first wage
knocks.says: (Holding a parcel badly.) “I bought my mum a kettle. With the first wage. I wanted somebody to see it before I posted it.”

answers.reply: “It whistles.” (It was enough.)

answers.say: Post it from the Front. It'll have a proper stamp.
answers.reply: “Can I?”

answers.say: D'you know where the money came from?
answers.reply: “…The bakery. I was on the bakery.” (He looks at the kettle.)

knocks.title: Somebody who believes it more
knocks.says: (A Grunt who joined for the Creed.) “I've read the notice on the door every morning for a month. Today we did the opposite. I'm not leaving. I'm asking you to read it again.”

answers.reply: “I didn't want to be.”
“It always is. That's on a lot of doors.”
“…To say what?”

knocks.title: Somebody who came for the wage
knocks.says: “I came for the dental. I'll be honest. But I heard the speech today and I— is it true? Any of it?”

answers.reply: “Blimey.”
“Which bit isn't?” (You may say, from the Ledger.)

answers.say: Does it matter, if the dental's real?
answers.reply: “It didn't yesterday.”

knocks.title: A challenge
knocks.says: “I'd like to fight you. Not for the chair. I want to know how far off I am.”

answers.reply: (A battle, three against three, at level. It's the Night's action.)
“That's not a number.”
“Otis doesn't fight. He stands in doors.” “Then get past him.”

knocks.title: “Train me.”
knocks.says: (A Grunt who's lost four in a row.) “I'm the worst in the building. Everyone's too kind to say. Train me, or tell me to go.”

answers.say: Six in the morning. The yard.
answers.reply: “…I didn't think you'd say yes.”

answers.say: You're not the worst. You're the newest.
answers.reply: “I've been here longer than Tobi.” “Tobi's lucky.”
(Their talent. They'd forgotten they had one.)

knocks.title: Something found, and not reported
knocks.says: “I found something at the Dig. It's small. It's old. I've not put it in the log. I wanted to hold it for a day first. Is that stealing?”

answers.reply: “Thank you. I'll log it Thursday.”
“Yes. Of course.” (He holds it a moment longer.)
(It's a tooth. Or a bead. Or a child's carved Pokémon, three thousand years old.)

knocks.title: Somebody who's frightened of it
knocks.says: (A Grunt on the Dig crew.) “The others won't say. I will. I don't want to be there when it wakes. I'll dig. I'll carry. I don't want to be in the room.”

answers.reply: “You'll put that on my card?” “Yes.”

answers.say: Nobody's making you look at it.
answers.reply: “It'll look at me.”
“Ask what we wanted. And we've forty answers.”

knocks.title: Somebody with nowhere else

who.outside: A stranger on the step, with a bag and no coat

knocks.says: “The woman at the ferry said you take people.”

answers.say: Come in. We'll sort the rest tomorrow.
answers.reply: “I can't do anything. I should say.” “Can you peel?” “…Yes.”
(One sentence. A flat that went, a job that went, a family that didn't.)
“Right. Sorry. She said— right.” (The door Grunt gives them the corridor floor anyway.)

knocks.title: “Can my brother stay?”
knocks.says: “My brother's eleven. Our nan's gone into hospital. Can he stay? He'd not be in it. He'd just be here.”

answers.say: Yes. He's Hortense's till your nan's out.
answers.reply: “He'll eat everything.”

answers.say: A base isn't a place for a child.
answers.reply: “No. Nor's an empty flat.”
(The district's Clinic, if there is one. If the team built it: “The one with our name on the bench.”)

knocks.title: “What happens when it's done?”
knocks.says: “When we've got them. When it's finished. What happens to us?”

answers.reply: “That's what I thought. I'd rather know you don't than think you do.”
“And I do what? I'm forty-four. I stand in doors.”
“…Another them? That's not a plan. That's a habit.”

knocks.title: Somebody who met the Target
knocks.says: “I met them. Today. By accident, in a queue. They held a door for me. They were— I'm sorry. They were nice.”

answers.say: They were nice to us once too.
answers.reply: “What changed?” (You may say, in a sentence.)

answers.say: It doesn't matter what they're like.
answers.reply: “It matters to what we're like.”
“It was a queue.”

knocks.title: The Pen: “How d'you sleep?”
knocks.says: (In the doorway of the Office, the Boss asks whoever runs the Pen: “How d'you sleep?” The answer's by their flaw.)

answers.reply: (They give it. The Boss runs the Pen now. “Since then” on each card is the Boss's to write.)
(They name someone. A Kind names themselves: “At least I'd mind.”)

answers.say: Send one home. You choose which.
answers.reply: (They choose. A Proud picks the Growlithe that cries, and says it's because of the noise.)

knocks.title: The Vault: Otis won't open it
knocks.says: (At the Office door, with the key on a string round his neck.) “You sent down for what's in the Vault. I'm not opening it. I'll give you the key and you can. I'm not.”

answers.reply: “Fourteen years. First door I've not opened.”
“Because I've heard it. Through the door. It's not right, what's in there.”
“…That I can do.”

knocks.title: The Infirmary: one of theirs
knocks.says: “There's a lad in bed four. He's not ours. He's one of theirs. He came in bleeding from the hand and the sign says ‘Anyone. No questions.’ So I've not asked. I'm telling you because he's in your building.”

answers.say: The sign says what it says.
answers.reply: “Good. I'd have ignored you otherwise.”
“That his hand hurts. I'll not have him questioned in a bed.”
“When he can hold a cup.” (A second sign under the first: “I mean it.”)

knocks.title: The Workshop: something nobody asked for
knocks.says: “I made something. Nobody asked. It's not for a job.” (A weather-vane with the team's letter on it; or a music box; or a latch for the Pen that opens from the inside.)

answers.say: Put it where people'll see it.
answers.reply: “It's only a— all right.”
“It's not for. That's what I liked.”
“You know what it does.” “Yes.”

knocks.title: The Listening Post: something private
knocks.says: “I heard something that isn't ours to hear. It's about one of us. It's not business. D'you want it?”

answers.reply: “Good. I've already forgotten it.”
“No. Somebody's in love.”
(She tells. Somebody's secret: a debt, a child, an exam they're sitting by post. Lux tells them she told.)

knocks.title: The Garage: teaching Beatriz to drive
knocks.says: “The kid wants to learn the van. Not for jobs. Round the yard. I said I'd ask.”

answers.reply: “I'll put cones out.”
“Fair enough. She'll learn somewhere worse.”
“My dad. In a milk float. I was nine.”

knocks.title: The Counting Room: the Boss's wage
knocks.says: “There's a wage on the sheet that's not been drawn in six weeks. It's yours.”

answers.reply: “I'll put it down as a loan from you to us, then. I'm not having it vanish.”
“In what name?” (You may type one, or not.)
“Among everyone? It's ₽14 a head.” “Among everyone.”

knocks.title: The Mess: somebody's not eating
knocks.says: “One of them's not eating. Three days. I'm not saying who till you say you'll not shout.”

answers.reply: (A name. Whoever's mood is lowest.)
“I have. It comes back.”
“Homesick. Or guilty. They look the same from a serving hatch.”

knocks.title: The Common Room: the door
knocks.says: (Whoever was last up.) “The Common Room door sticks. Otis says take it off. Hortense says a room wants a door. They've sent me because neither'll come.”

answers.reply: “Hortense'll say she told you.”
“Faye's got a plane.”
“I think I've never been asked what I think about a door.”

knocks.title: The Wall: something's been taken down
knocks.says: “Somebody's taken the cutting down. The one about the docks. It wasn't me. It's not a good cutting. But it happened.”

answers.reply: “I'll need to find it.” (It's in someone's locker.)
“Then the Wall's only the nice ones.”
“Faye. She was on the docks. She won't say.”

knocks.title: The cat
knocks.says: (The door Grunt.) “There's a cat. It came in with the coal. Is it ours?”

answers.reply: “What's it called?” (Type it, or leave it to a vote.)
“Nobody's. I asked down the street.”
“I'll put it out.” (They don't. It's in the Garage. Tomasz feeds it.)

knocks.title: The Long Window
knocks.says: (Somebody passing the Office door late, who stops.) “You've been stood there an hour. …Can you see the Centre from here? I never knew that.”

answers.reply: (They do. They point out their own street, or where it'd be.)

answers.say: What d'you see when you look out?
answers.reply: (By flaw. A Proud: “What we've got.” A Kind: “Who's still got their lights on.”)
“You as well.” (They're right.)

knocks.title: Skims, again
knocks.says: “You told me to ask. I'm asking. It's four hundred this time. I'll tell you what it's for if you want. I'd rather you didn't want.” (Off the money since the first time: “I've been honest for a region. It's been awful. I'd like to be trusted with it again and see if I can do it on purpose.”)

answers.say: Take it. I don't need to know.
answers.reply: “…It's not for me. I'll say that much.”
(He says. His sister. Then her landlord. He's been paying a stranger's rent since Region 1.)
“No. Right. That's allowed.”

knocks.title: Drinks, again
knocks.says: (Sober, at an odd hour.) “It's a month. I've not said. I'm saying to you because you've got the bottle and you've never once looked at the drawer when I've come in.”

answers.reply: “It is.”

answers.say: (Open the drawer. Give it back.) It's yours. Whether you open it's yours too.
answers.reply: (He takes it. He puts it on the Common Room shelf, sealed, in full view.)

answers.say: And the one in the cistern?
answers.reply: “Hortense found it. She made a trifle.”

knocks.title: Doubts, again
knocks.says: “I stopped again. This time I was right. There was a child asleep in the back room. I'd like it noted that I was right, because I never know.”

answers.say: Noted. In the Log. In your name.
answers.reply: “In my name?”
“Probably. I'd still stop.”
“I don't. I stop when I'd be ashamed to keep going. It's not a method.”

knocks.title: Talks, again
knocks.says: “I've been at the pub. I didn't say anything. I heard something.”

answers.reply: (A fact about the neighbour: a tick's day; who their handler's seeing.)
“A lad from theirs. He talks more than me.”

answers.say: Did you buy him a drink?
answers.reply: “Three.” (Ngozi puts three drinks on the Ledger under “Intelligence”.)

knocks.title: Loves someone on the other side, again
knocks.says: “She knows. I told her. She's not gone to her sergeant. She's asked to meet you.”

answers.reply: “In uniform?” “In a coat.”
“I'll tell her you said that kindly.”
“To know if she'd have to arrest me. I said I didn't know.”

knocks.title: Proud, again
knocks.says: “I've made an error. In the Ledger. ₽3,000, three weeks back. Nobody's caught it. Nobody would. I've come to say so before I correct it, because I'd not have believed me if I'd only said after.”

answers.reply: “That's all?” “That's all.”
“Because I'd know.”
“That's what I can't stand.”

knocks.title: Kind, again
knocks.says: “I've been sending the leftovers down to the shelter. Out the back. Every night since the first town. I've come to tell you it's about a tenth of the food bill.”

answers.say: Put it on the Ledger. As a Work.
answers.reply: “It's soup.” “It's a Work.”
“…I'll need another pan.”
“No.” (That's the whole answer. It doesn't stop.)

knocks.title: Freezes
knocks.says: “I didn't move. At the lookout. I saw them coming and I didn't whistle. I know I'm only on lookouts. I can't even do the one thing.”

answers.reply: (Everything. How many, which way, what they carried. She froze and she saw it all.)
“Drop—” “Anything. A noise is a noise.”
“What's left?” (The map table. She's better at it.)

knocks.title: Voice: the speech she didn't give
knocks.says: “I'd a woman at the door today I could've talked round in a minute. I didn't. I told her to keep her shop. I don't know what came over me.”

answers.reply: “It cost us a holding.” “I can count.”
“She'd my mother's hands.”
“I'll go. I'll not do it well.”

knocks.title: Hands: the lock she couldn't
knocks.says: “There's a lock in this town I can't do. Four tries. I'm telling you because I've never said that sentence.”

answers.reply: “A locksmith's. Retired. It's on his own front door. I think it's a joke.”
“I know we go round.”
(She does. It doesn't open. A note's pushed under it from inside: “Nearly.”)

knocks.title: Eyes: something she wishes she'd not seen
knocks.says: “I saw the kid's mum today. Through the long lens. Hanging washing. I wasn't looking for her. I've not been able to un-see it.”

answers.say: Take the lens off that street.
answers.reply: “For good?” “For good.”
“She pegs from the left. She talks to the Pidgey.”
“It's somebody's back garden.”

knocks.title: Nerve: afraid for somebody else
knocks.says: “I'm not scared of the kid. I'm scared for the kid. They went into the other lot's place on their own today. I watched them go in. I nearly followed.”

answers.reply: “As what?” “As a bloke who happened to be passing.”
“They're a kid.”
“Because I'd not asked you.”

knocks.title: Books: a number that's a person
knocks.says: “Line forty in the Ledger's been paying since the first week. Never late. Today it's short by eleven. In thirty years, when a good payer's short by eleven, somebody's died or somebody's been born.”

answers.reply: “I have. It's born. A girl.”
“It is. I'll chase it.” (He doesn't. He pays the eleven himself.)
“Three Bosses. You learn what the numbers are about.”

knocks.title: Wheels: the road not taken
knocks.says: “There's a road out of this region the maps don't have. I found it Sunday. I've not told the neighbour and I've not told the police. I'm telling you third. I could've told you first.”

answers.reply: “…I thought you'd be angry.”
“The old lady. It goes past hers.”
“Who'd I tell?” (He tells Tomasz, who's thrilled.)

knocks.title: Heart: the one she couldn't mend
knocks.says: “There's a Grunt I can't fix. Nothing's broken. They're sad, and I've no bandage for it. I'm reporting a patient I can't treat.”

answers.reply: (A name. The lowest mood on the Roster.)
“A week at home. Or one good job. They'd know which.”
“It's the only one I've got.” (She tries anyway.)

knocks.title: A Grunt's first week
knocks.says: (Somebody hired four days ago.) “I don't know where anything is. I don't know who to ask. I've been using the wrong mug since Tuesday and somebody's been letting me.”

answers.reply: “Otis's.”
“Everything?” “She'll tell you when it's not hers to answer.”
“Tobi did. He got lost.”

knocks.title: Passed over
knocks.says: (Somebody who's done three jobs well and watched a newer Grunt made Lead.) “I'm not asking for it. I'm asking what I did.”

answers.reply: “Right. That's fair.” (Or, if you just picked: “So nothing. I did nothing.”)
“I'll hold you to it.”
“…No. I want to have been asked.”

knocks.title: A Lead who lost one
knocks.says: (Still in their coat.) “We lost the job. It was me. I called it early. I'd like you to hear it from me before you read it on the Board.”

answers.reply: (One thing. It's the job's Not-known field, learned.)

answers.say: It was the odds. I set them.
answers.reply: “You printed them. I read them. I still called it early.”
“I know. I wanted it said out loud as well.”

knocks.title: A Specialist disagrees
knocks.says: “You were wrong today. It's my talent, so I'm saying it. I'd not be any use to you if I didn't.”

answers.reply: “…Thank you.” (They can be made Officer.)

answers.say: I hear you. I'd do it again.
answers.reply: “Then I've said it and you've heard it. That's what I came for.”
“It's exactly mine. It's my talent.”

knocks.title: An Executive reports: a mercy
knocks.says: “I let the cannery off the month. You weren't here. They'd had a fire. I'm not asking; I'm telling you what I did with your name.”

answers.reply: “I thought you'd say that. I'd have done it if you wouldn't.”
“There wasn't a next time. There was a fire.”
“₽900 and nothing.” (Ngozi's put it under “Weather”.)

knocks.title: An Executive reports: something you wouldn't have done
knocks.says: “I Leaned on the ferryman. You've never Leaned on anyone. I know. It was that or lose the launch. I'd like you to say what you'd have done, so I know for next time.”

answers.reply: “…Then I'll go and see him tomorrow.”
“You've never said that before.”
“‘I knew you lot'd get round to it.’”

knocks.title: A feud
knocks.says: (Two people in the doorway at once, not looking at each other.) “You say.” “No, you say.”

answers.say: One at a time. You first.
answers.reply: (The first's version. Then the second's. They don't match, and neither's lying.)

answers.say: I'm not settling it. You are. Common Room. Now.
answers.reply: “With the door shut?”
(They take it.)

knocks.title: Friends
knocks.says: (Two Grunts.) “Can we be on the same squad? We're better together. We've no proof. We just are.”

answers.reply: “Told you they'd say yes.” “You said they'd say no.”
“How?” “One job. Tomorrow. I'll watch the odds.”
“We do that anyway. Across the yard. It's worse.”

knocks.title: A letter from a garrison

who.outside: A letter, from a garrison

knocks.says: “Boss. It's quiet here. That's the report. Unofficially: the baker's daughter's teaching Dov to read music and he's dreadful. We've mended the fence at the allotments without being asked. Is that all right? We weren't sure if we were still yours.”

answers.reply: (The garrison does one small Work a district, unasked, free.)
(It holds. The next letter's two sentences.)
(They do. The district's held by nobody.)

knocks.title: Poached
knocks.says: (Somebody good.) “Theirs have offered me double. I've not said yes. I've not said no. I thought you should get to say something.”

answers.reply: “Stay. I wanted to hear if you'd ask or just match it.”
“Then I'm worth double. I'd wondered.”
“…I didn't think you'd make it easy.”

knocks.title: Faye, after the list
knocks.says: “You put my name on a list of people who get to live. I didn't ask. Who's the baker in Camphrier? She's on it too. She paid five million. We got on for nothing. I'd like off.”

answers.say: I'll take all of us off.
answers.reply: “He'll not like that.” “No.”
“From what? What's coming that you've made a list for?”
“Just mine?” (She looks at the door.) “…Do Hortense's too. She'd not want it.”

knocks.title: The laundress

who.outside: A woman with soot on her apron, who's walked three miles

knocks.says: “I'd a mangle. I'd forty sheets on the line and a copper on the boil. There's a wall on it. A castle wall. I pay you every Friday so that this sort of thing doesn't happen. So.”

answers.reply: “A mangle, a copper, a yard, and whoever did it told off.”
“I know it wasn't you. You're who I pay.”
“I've not come to eat.” (She eats.)

knocks.title: Plumeria at the door

who.outside: Plumeria, alone, soaked

knocks.says: “I don't know who else has got a van.”

answers.reply: “…That's it? I'd a whole thing about how I'd owe you.”
“To be somewhere he can see when he comes back out. That's all. I can't do anything. I can be there.”
“I know what we are. I'm stood here anyway.”

knocks.title: A boy in a hood
knocks.says: (The door Grunt, at the Office.) “There's a lad at the front asking if we're hiring. Hood up. Got a— I don't know what it is. It's got a helmet on. I said ‘How old are you?’ and he said ‘Old enough’ and I gave him a sandwich. He's eating it on the step. What do I tell him?”

answers.say: Tell him no. Tell him there's a sandwich any night.
answers.reply: “He'll not come back. Proud.” (He comes back twice. For the sandwich.)

answers.say: Ask him what he's running from.
answers.reply: “I did. He said, ‘My mother.’ I said, ‘Aren't we all,’ and he nearly laughed.”
“I don't think it's a home.”

knocks.title: The stipend

who.outside: Whoever's been paying the Digs

knocks.says: (The Digs have had ₽800 a day from somebody since the first region. Tonight, who. The Patron: “It was me. I wanted to see one done properly before I died. Don't look like that; I'm in excellent health. It's my pension.” Or the neighbour's memo: “The calculation has always included your excavations. Kindly continue.” Or a university's secretary: “There's a form. It's forty pages. Section nine asks what you intend to do with it.”)

answers.reply: (It goes on. ₽800 a day.)
(It stops.)

answers.say: Pay it back. Honestly. (Send the log, uncut; or fill in the form honestly.)
answers.reply: (Chidi fills in section nine. The Scheme screen's sentence gets plainer.)

knocks.title: Proton asks for a job

who.outside: Proton, very polite

knocks.says: “I've a great deal of experience. I'm told you're short of people who'll do the unpleasant part. I'm the unpleasant part.”

answers.reply: “You'll want me before the end.”
(He tells it. Without flinching. It's the whole reason.)
(Otis:) “Out.” (That's all.)

knocks.title: One of theirs wants in

who.outside: A neighbour's Grunt, in half a uniform

knocks.says: “I'd like to change sides. I'm not bringing anything. I've no secrets. I'm just not— I looked at what we did Tuesday and I'm not doing Wednesday.”

answers.reply: (The neighbour's last tick, from inside.)
“Yours gave my mate a bandage.” (Or: “You're nearest.”)
“Which one?”

knocks.title: A Boss, asking to be a Grunt

who.outside: A fallen Boss, without the bandana, holding it

knocks.says: “I'd like to find out what I was asking of them. I've never been told what to do in my life. I'd like to see what it's like. I'll take the worst bunk.”

answers.reply: “A line. Right. …‘Won't flood anything.’”
“You beat me, or the kid did, and you didn't crow. I noticed.”

answers.say: No. Go and make it right where you did it.
answers.reply: “…That's harder.” “Yes.”

knocks.title: The handler Admin

who.outside: The neighbour's handler Admin

knocks.says: “I'm told to tell you where we stand. I'd rather tell you where I stand. They're not the same.”

answers.reply: (One sentence their Boss wouldn't like. It's the Betrayer's tell, a district early.)

answers.say: Say what you were sent to say.
answers.reply: (The stance, as it is.)
“…Ask me after.”

knocks.title: Three people and a Meowth

who.outside: Three people and a Meowth, all at once, with a motto

knocks.says: (A motto.) (The door Grunt:) “I asked what they can do. That was the answer. It rhymed.”

answers.reply: “Between us?” “There's a pay rise for the Meowth?” “There's no Meowth on the sheet.” “I'm on the sheet!”

answers.say: What happened to your last job?
answers.reply: “We were let go.” “We let ourselves go.” “The boss stopped answering.”
“We'll try again tomorrow!” (They do.)

knocks.title: After a war: somebody left behind
knocks.says: (The door Grunt.) “There's one of theirs sat on the step. The rest've gone. Nobody came back for him. He's not asking for anything. He's just sat.”

answers.say: Bring him in. Feed him. Send him home with the fare.
answers.reply: “Home's two regions off.” “Then it's a big fare.”

answers.say: Ask him why nobody came back.
answers.reply: “He says they counted and went. He says he's never been good at being counted.”
“No.” (The door Grunt takes him a blanket.)

knocks.title: “That's what it's like, then.”
knocks.says: (With the Card.) “‘Takes: one Sneasel. From: a Grunt, on Market Street. How it's written down: stock.’ …I've filled in forty of these. I never once read one from this end.”

answers.reply: “And the next person's? Who gets theirs back?”
“I always knew. I'd not felt it.”
“Needle. She steals my socks.”

knocks.title: The landlord

who.outside: A man with a folder

knocks.says: “You've been in my building six weeks. I've had no rent, three complaints, and a very polite note from a Mr. Blackthorn telling me not to come round. I've come round.”

answers.reply: (A fair figure. He's surprised to be asked.)
“Singing. A van. A cat.” (The singing's the Roster's. It's on Sundays. He's invited.)

answers.say: Mr. Blackthorn will see you out.
answers.reply: “I thought he might.”

knocks.title: A Leader walks in

who.outside: A Gym Leader, alone, at the front door

knocks.says: (What they say is by how their Gym was got. Beat: “I've come for a rematch. Not for the Gym. For me.” Bought: “I've brought it back. All of it. I've not slept.” Bent: “I've come to see what I bent for.” Replaced, the old Leader: “Who's in my Gym? Are they kind to the trainees?” Befriended: “I was passing.” Left alone: “You've held eleven of my twelve streets and never once come up the hill. I've come down it. Why not?”)

answers.say: (Meet them: a fight; take it back; walk them round; the truth.)
answers.reply: (It's their line at the gate on the Reckoning's last day.)
(They stay an hour.)
(They go. It's still their line at the gate.)

knocks.title: A constable, with a warning

who.outside: A constable, out of uniform, not coming in

knocks.says: “Tomorrow. Early. I'm not here. I was never here. I'd move the old man and the girl tonight if I were you.”

answers.reply: (By who. “She asked me to.” “I've been writing reports on you for a year.” “My mum's got a roof.”)
“Don't.”
(The detective's name.) “They don't want to. I'll say that.”

knocks.title: The detective, a second time

who.outside: The detective, hat in hand

knocks.says: “I've a warrant in my pocket I've not served. I wanted to give you a day. I don't know why. That's what I've come to say. That I don't know why.”

answers.say: I do. (Because of the bakery. Because you've seen the kitchen. Because you're tired.)
answers.reply: “…Perhaps.”
“Tomorrow.”
(They sit. Nobody says anything for a while.)

knocks.title: Somebody from the paper

who.outside: A reporter

knocks.says: “I'm doing a piece. ‘Who are they?’ I've three people who say you mended the bridge and three who say you run the docks. I can print both. I'd rather print what's true.”

answers.reply: “On the record?” “On the record.”
“And the docks?” (A silence.)
“That's what the docks said.”

knocks.title: Somebody returning something

who.outside: A girl of ten, with her dad behind her

knocks.says: “Your Rattata was in our shed. It's had some cheese. Dad says I've to bring it back and not ask questions. Why's it got a number?”

answers.say: It hasn't, now. What'd you call it?
answers.reply: “Cheese.”
(Her dad:) “I've not seen anything. She's not been here.”
“Can I?”

knocks.title: Somebody whose Pokémon's in the Pen

who.outside: A man, with a child of nine holding his hand

knocks.says: “This is Tam. She's got something to ask you. I told her you'd not see us. She said you would.” (Tam Okonkwo:) “Have you got Biscuit?”

answers.reply: (The Boss goes and gets him. The latch. The card comes off the door.)
(Tam:) “He's barking. I can hear him.” (He is.)

answers.say: Who told you he was here?
answers.reply: (Her dad:) “A lass with a toolbag. Knocked, said one thing, went.”

knocks.title: Somebody who wants to pay

who.outside: The baker

knocks.says: “You waived us. In the spring. I've had a good summer. I've brought what I'd have owed. I don't like owing, even to people who say I don't.”

answers.reply: “I've got an oven.” “A better one.”
“That's nearly fair.”
“Good. Now we're straight.”

knocks.title: The Friend, with a letter

who.outside: The Hero's Friend

knocks.says: “I've a letter for whoever runs this. I'm to give it to them and not read it. I've not read it. It's from a friend of mine. I don't know why they're writing to you.”

answers.reply: (It's the Hero's question, the one their reason's made of, asked to a stranger.)

answers.say: (Give it back unread.) Tell them to ask me themselves.
answers.reply: (The next fire opens with it.)
“The one who's in charge of the soup? No? …Oh. Oh.”

knocks.title: The Rival, wanting a battle

who.outside: The Hero's Rival, at the front door, loud

knocks.says: “I'm not the one you're worried about. I know that. I'd like to be. Fight me.”

answers.reply: (Win: they're insufferable about how close it was. Lose: they tell the Hero, “I beat their Boss,” and the Hero doesn't believe them.)

answers.say: Not tonight. Come in and eat.
answers.reply: (They eat. They don't stop talking.) (Tobi:) “Can we keep this one?”
“…Them. They walk into places on their own.”

knocks.title: The Stray: “Is this yours?”

who.outside: The Hero's Stray, holding something

knocks.says: “Oh. Hello. Sorry. Is this yours?” (A dropped Card, a kit Pokémon, the weather-vane, the cat.)

answers.reply: (If it's a Card, they've read it.) “It says the odds on it. And who won't go. Do they all say that?”
“By the thing I was looking for. Which wasn't there. But this was.”
“Oh. No, I couldn't. It's got a name on.” (They put it on the step and go.)

knocks.title: A Grunt who's been writing to the Hero
knocks.says: “I've been writing to the kid. Since they beat me at the gate. They write back. I've not said anything about us. We write about vans. Is that— am I in trouble?”

answers.reply: “I'd have stopped if you'd said.” “I know. Don't.”

answers.say: What do they say about us?
answers.reply: “Nothing. They ask if I'm all right.”
“Right.” (He stops.)

knocks.title: Kanto: the lodge

who.outside: A very old Chansey, with a warden's tag

knocks.says: (The yard gate. It's come for its rounds. Nobody's told it the Safari's shut.)

answers.reply: (It checks every Pokémon in the yard, every night, for the region. Halima takes notes.)
(A name, and “Property of the Warden.” The Warden, in Fuchsia, thought it had died.)
(It waits. It's there in the morning.)

knocks.title: Johto: the basement
knocks.says: (Not a knock. Something on the cellar stair. It's looking. It's burned along one side, long ago, and it's not hurt, and it's not afraid.)

answers.reply: (It looks. It goes down again. The basement's left alone.)
(Three rooms nobody's mapped, and a fourth it won't let be entered.)
(A noise, some nights. The door Grunt asks to be moved.)

knocks.title: Hoenn: a trade

who.outside: A child, at the mouth of the tree

knocks.says: “Your base is boring. I'll swap you a Skitty cushion for that lamp. Everyone swaps. Don't you know how it works?”

answers.reply: (A Skitty cushion in the Office. The child tells everyone the base is “all right, a bit grey.”)
(A poster, a tyre, a brick that's “really heavy.” It looks dreadful and the Roster loves it.)

answers.say: This isn't that kind of base.
answers.reply: “Then why's it in a tree?” (It's a fair point.)

knocks.title: Sinnoh: decorating advice

who.outside: The Underground Man, uninvited, looking at the tunnel

knocks.says: “No, no, no. You've put your Vault where anyone'd look. And where's your flag? You must have a flag.”

answers.reply: (He says. The Vault's moved one square, and it's better.)
“Then I shall bring you one.” (He does. The team's letter, hand-sewn, wrong colour.)
“My dear, I dug it.”

knocks.title: Unova: the timetable
knocks.says: (An envelope under the carriage door. Inside: a printed sheet. “Inspections, Line 7 (disused). All times exact.” And, in two different hands: “Mind the gap.” “All aboard.”)

answers.reply: (The base can't be found by an inspection.)
(A second envelope: two tickets for the Battle Subway.)
(The one shunt, used. A third envelope arrives at the new siding. They knew that too.)

knocks.title: Kalos: the owner comes home

who.outside: A woman with a great many cases, in the yard, at two in the morning

knocks.says: “Who on earth are you? This is my servants' wing. …Is that soup? I've not had a hot meal since Lumiose.”

answers.reply: (She believes it. She asks for breakfast at eight. Otis buttles. He's superb.)

answers.say: We're a team. We've been living in your wing.
answers.reply: “A team of what?” (The Creed's line.) “…How thrilling. Do go on. Nobody tells me anything.”
“Don't be absurd. Who'd make the soup?”

knocks.title: Alola: the Mimikyu
knocks.says: (The stock's been moved again. Every tin in the Mess is facing the wall. In the middle of the floor: a rag, with a drawn-on face, very still.)

answers.say: (Sit down near it. Not too near.)
answers.reply: (It stays. It's the base's, not the team's.)
(They're turned again by morning.)
“It likes you. It doesn't like many people. Don't make it sad or I'll know.”

knocks.title: Galar: the lock-keeper

who.outside: An old man with a windlass

knocks.says: “You've been moored on my pound a week. I've let you through eleven locks and you've not once said good morning. That's all I've come about. Good morning's free.”

answers.reply: “There. Was that hard?”
(He's aboard an hour. He names every boat that's ever carried anything it shouldn't.)
“On a canal? Good luck.”

knocks.title: Paldea: sandwiches

who.outside: A woman from down the hill, with a covered plate

knocks.says: “You're the new people in the lighthouse. I'm at the bottom. I've made too many. My youngest's just set off on the Treasure Hunt and I keep cooking for two.” (She's the Hero's mother. She doesn't know. The Boss does: it's in the File.)

answers.reply: (She comes up every few days.)

answers.say: I think I should tell you who we are.
answers.reply: (The Creed's line. She listens.) “…Well. You'll still want feeding.”
“I'll leave them on the step.” (The door Grunt's been eating them and saying nothing.)
